gloss: Having a well-thought-out plan or preparation.
teaser: Ever wondered how to express confidence in your plans? Let's dive into this idiom!
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how to express confidence in your plans? Let's dive into this idiom! [break 1s] The phrase is: 胸有成竹, xiōng yǒu chéng zhú. [break 1s] 胸 (xiōng) - chest, heart [break 0.5s] 有 (yǒu) - to have [break 0.5s] 成 (chéng) - to succeed, to complete [break 0.5s] 竹 (zhú) - bamboo [break 0.5s] The full idiom again: 胸有成竹, which literally means "having bamboo in one's chest" and figuratively means having a well-thought-out plan or preparation. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a painter during the Song Dynasty who was known for his incredible skill in painting bamboo. He would visualize the bamboo in his mind before he even picked up the brush, showcasing his preparation and confidence. As a result, the phrase came to symbolize the importance of having a clear plan before taking action. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他在考试前复习得很充分, 胸有成竹. [break 1s] He reviewed thoroughly before the exam, feeling confident and well-prepared. [break 1s] Example 2: 这个项目经理做了详细的计划, 所以他在会议上胸有成竹. [break 1s] The project manager made detailed plans, so he was confident during the meeting. [break 1s] Example 3: 她在演讲前准备了很久, 胸有成竹地走上了舞台. [break 1s] She prepared for a long time before the speech, confidently stepping onto the stage. [break 1s] So that's 胸有成竹, which means having a well-thought-out plan or preparation. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
